verdict.summary: There's no self-serve console. You get an OAuth client ID and secret only by submitting Dialpad's Jira registration form, and any scope beyond basic access (recordings, SMS content, call list, refresh tokens) has to be approved by Dialpad over email. Once you have credentials, the flow itself is standard OAuth 2.0 with PKCE, and the same sandbox and production hosts work for any Dialpad user.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Most of this is waiting for Dialpad to process the registration form and issue credentials; the docs give no turnaround time.

timeToProd.assumes: A production OAuth client with extra scopes an agent needs (calls:list, recordings_export, message_content_export, offline_access) approved by Dialpad; basic-access-only clients skip the scope approval, and a Marketplace listing is a separate optional request.
timeToProd.waitingOn: Dialpad issuing the client after the registration form, and email approval of special scopes (api@dialpad.com).

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Manual registration and scope approval are sourced; no durations are published, so the range is our estimate.

verdict.cost: Not stated; testing realistically needs access to a Dialpad company account (sandbox or paid).

prerequisites.item: A completed OAuth app registration form (redirect URIs, special scopes)
prerequisites.why: Dialpad issues the client ID and secret only after you submit this form.

prerequisites.item: A Dialpad account to test against (sandbox.dialpad.com or dialpad.com)
prerequisites.why: The authorize endpoint requires a Dialpad login before the consent screen.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: Both sandbox and production /oauth2/authorize redirected to /login on 2026-10-20.

prerequisites.item: A redirect URI without a # fragment
prerequisites.why: Redirect URIs may include query parameters but must not contain a fragment.

scopeTiers.impact: Default user-level access to the authorizing user's Dialpad account; still needs the manual client registration.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: reviewRequired=true reflects the manual registration, not a scope review.

scopeTiers.impact: Needed to list calls, get recording URLs in call events, export a user's SMS text, and keep access with refresh tokens. Scopes must be approved by Dialpad.
Company-wide SMS content and admin endpoints; some API reference entries say they need a company admin API key.

steps.title: Decide scopes and redirect URIs
steps.detail: List the special scopes your agent needs (calls:list, recordings_export, message_content_export, offline_access) and every redirect URI for sandbox and production.

steps.title: Draft the registration and scope justifications
steps.detail: Write a short description of the app and why each special scope is needed, to paste into the form and the api@dialpad.com email.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: The form's exact fields weren't visible to us.

steps.title: Submit the OAuth registration form
steps.detail: Submit Dialpad's Jira registration form with redirect URIs and special scopes.

steps.title: Wait for client credentials
steps.detail: Dialpad provides the client ID and secret after registration.

steps.title: Request special-scope approval if not already granted
steps.detail: Email api@dialpad.com to get the extra scopes approved for your client.

steps.title: Implement the authorization code flow with PKCE
steps.detail: Redirect to https://dialpad.com/oauth2/authorize (or sandbox.dialpad.com) with response_type=code, client_id, redirect_uri, state, scope and code_challenge. Exchange the code within 1 minute at POST /oauth2/token with code_verifier.

steps.title: Add refresh and deauthorize handling
steps.detail: With offline_access, refresh via grant_type=refresh_token and store the new refresh token returned. On disconnect, delete event subscriptions, then POST /oauth2/deauthorize with the bearer token.

steps.title: Build rate-limit handling
steps.detail: Stay under 20 requests/second per company and the per-API caps (e.g. initiate calls 5/min per user target, send SMS 100/min).

steps.title: Test in sandbox, then switch hosts to production
steps.detail: Run the flow on sandbox.dialpad.com, then against dialpad.com with a production user from another company.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Whether sandbox and production need separate client registrations isn't stated.

steps.title: Optional: request a Marketplace listing
steps.detail: Complete the requirements in Dialpad's publish request form to appear in the Dialpad App Marketplace.

agentCanDo: Pick the minimal special scopes and draft justifications
Implement the code flow with PKCE, refresh and deauthorize
Build per-company and per-API rate-limit handling
Check endpoints such as the OIDC discovery document and token endpoint
humanMustDo: Submit the Jira registration form and receive the client secret
Obtain a Dialpad sandbox or company account for testing
Request a Marketplace listing if wanted

blockers.symptom: No 'create app' button anywhere on developers.dialpad.com
blockers.cause: Dialpad doesn't offer self-serve OAuth client creation; clients are issued after the registration form.
blockers.fix: Submit the Jira registration form and wait for credentials.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Docs describe only the form; absence of a console is our inference.

blockers.symptom: Requested scope rejected or missing from the token
blockers.cause: The special scope hasn't been approved for your client.
blockers.fix: Email api@dialpad.com to get it approved, then re-request.

blockers.symptom: Token exchange fails with an invalid/expired code
blockers.cause: Authorization codes are valid for only 1 minute.
blockers.fix: Exchange the code immediately in the callback handler.

blockers.symptom: Token call returns {"exception":"bad_request","message":"{'code': ['Missing data for required field.']}"}
blockers.cause: Required fields (code, client credentials, redirect_uri) missing from the token request.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: Observed with a POST containing only grant_type on 2026-10-20.

blockers.symptom: Users must reconnect after the access token expires
blockers.cause: offline_access wasn't requested or approved, so no refresh token was issued.
blockers.fix: Get offline_access approved and include it in the scope parameter.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: The access token lifetime isn't stated in the docs.

nuances.text: Dialpad recommends OAuth only for apps used across multiple companies; admins integrating their own company can generate an API key instead.

Rate limits are 20 requests/second per company, plus per-API caps (create contacts 100/min, initiate calls 5/min per user target, send SMS 100/min, callrouter updates 1 per 5 min). Many API reference entries also list 1200/min.
The access token lifetime isn't documented; the refresh example shows an expires_in value that looks like a Unix timestamp rather than seconds, so handle both.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: The example value 1680047149 is our basis for this reading.

nuances.text: Refresh returns a new refresh token too, so persist it each time.
Dialpad publishes an OIDC discovery document (PKCE S256 and plain, refresh_token grant, claims sub/email/given_name/family_name).
